name:        createReorderable
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core
description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook createReorderable

name:        useScrollLock
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useScrollLock

name:        useTreeFocus
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Manages roving-tabindex focus and the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model. ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End roam linearly over the visible treeitems (skipping disabled ones), while ArrowRight/ArrowLeft carry tree semantics (expand/collapse, move to first-child/parent). Enter/Space activate, and printable characters trigger typeahead.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTreeFocus
